findings.title: Calculated recommendation claims omit required structured provenance
findings.what: These return objects publish token, cost, session, or model-price claims but provide no structured provenance identifying their source artifacts and fields. Human-readable evidence strings and reclaim metadata do not provide the required reproducible observation records.
findings.fix: Add provenance observations for every material claim, naming the precise parsed source and field, recording calculated values and inference, and including an as-of date wherever the source is historical.
findings.acceptance: For representative emitted recommendations from all four detectors, the repository provenance validator reports no errors and tests assert the exact source, field, value, inference, and applicable asOf fields.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read each complete returned recommendation object at the cited lines. None contains a provenance property; comparison support was limited to the batch's edit-format-churn and local-downroute implementations, which demonstrate structured observations and asOf handling.

findings.title: Agent-type detector makes an unsupported recovery claim and offers a blanket validated pin
findings.what: The code explicitly says it has no scoped, quality-backed model-right-sizing claim and books a flag-only reclaim, but the detail says right-sizing recovers most cost. Its fix then emits a top-level settings.json model pin, which changes all routed work rather than only the flagged agent type; without fixKind, it is treated as validated.
findings.fix: Remove the recovery assertion unless quality and scoped-cost evidence is available. Replace the blanket snippet with an actually agent-scoped configuration, or mark it illustrative and clearly require adaptation.
findings.acceptance: A test with only aggregate mean-cost evidence emits no quantified/majority recovery claim; fix validation identifies the snippet as agent-scoped, or effectiveFixKind returns illustrative for the blanket example.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed lines 31-33 disclaim the necessary evidence, line 48 still asserts recovery of most cost, and lines 55-59 provide a top-level model setting with no illustrative classification. The batch test only checks that the snippet contains Haiku and does not invalidate the defect.

findings.title: Expensive-session detector equates observed spend with recoverable savings
findings.what: top3Cost is the full observed cost of the three most expensive sessions. Assigning it directly to estSavingsUsd assumes the proposed scoping guidance eliminates 100% of those sessions' spend, although the detector measures neither waste nor a counterfactual avoidable fraction.
findings.fix: Keep top3Cost as accounting evidence only. Remove estSavingsUsd, or calculate savings from a separately evidenced and conservative counterfactual with explicit provenance.
findings.acceptance: A concentration-only fixture still reports observed top-three cost/share but has no estSavingsUsd; alternatively, a counterfactual fixture proves the emitted savings from cited fields and never books the full necessary session cost as avoidable.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-derived lines 20-25 and confirmed top3Cost is a direct sum of observed estimatedCost. Line 36 copies that entire sum into savings without any waste classifier, baseline, experiment, or recovery fraction.

findings.title: Historical idle-tool evidence is presented without a date and includes an unobserved token range
findings.what: The implementation acknowledges that tool inventory is historical, but the recommendation and provenance contain no asOf value. It also claims every idle tool adds approximately 50–200 tokens per turn, while the cited aggregate inventory fields only establish loaded/used counts and do not measure manifest token size.
findings.fix: Carry the inventory observation date into provenance and rendered copy, demoting or suppressing undated/stale data. Cite a measured manifest-token field for overhead, or remove the numeric 50–200 range and state only the observed utilization fact.
findings.acceptance: A dated inventory renders 'as of YYYY-MM-DD' and sets provenance.asOf/stale appropriately; an undated inventory cannot emit a present-tense claim; no numeric token range appears unless an observation cites the field containing that measurement.
findings.verifyNote: Adversarial re-read confirmed the historical-data acknowledgment at lines 28-32, no asOf in the provenance at lines 73-91, and no observation supporting the numeric range repeated at lines 67 and 90. Current-config reconciliation does not date the historical utilization evidence.

findings.title: Flagged-session aggregation is quadratic in session count
findings.what: The detector reduces over every tokenData row and calls flagged.some for each row. When many sessions are flagged, membership work grows as O(tokenData.length × flagged.length).
findings.fix: Build a Set of flagged session IDs during the first pass, or accumulate flagged totalOutput directly when pushing each flagged row, then compute totalOutput in O(n).
findings.acceptance: A regression test or probe with increasing all-flagged session counts demonstrates linear membership work, and the resulting totalOutput, reclaim fraction, and savings remain unchanged.
findings.verifyNote: Second pass re-read the first traversal and cited aggregation. flagged can grow to tokenData length, and Array.some is invoked once for every tokenData row, so the worst case is reproducibly quadratic.
